_meta.purpose: Ground-truth reference set for validating the stem-loop RT-qPCR primer designer.
_meta.design_is_deterministic_note: For Chen-2005 stem-loop RT-qPCR, two of the three primers are fully determined by the mature miRNA sequence: (1) the RT stem-loop primer = fixed universal body + reverse-complement of the 3'-terminal 6 nt; (2) the universal reverse primer is a fixed constant. The forward primer's specific region equals the 5' prefix of the miRNA. The validator recomputes these expected values independently from the SAME sequence the tool used (returned in metadata.mirna_sequence), so results do not depend on any hand-entered sequence.
sources: [Chen05] Chen C et al. Nucleic Acids Res. 2005;33(20):e179 — original stem-loop RT-qPCR; RT primer hybridizes 6-8 nt at 3' end of mature miRNA.

[Wang17] Wang Y et al. Mol Med Rep. 2017;17(3):3690-3696. DOI 10.3892/mmr.2017.8297 (PubMed PMID 29257343) — let-7 members share 16 identical 5' nt; single-nucleotide discrimination; amplification efficiency 0.93-1.14.
[Var07] Varkonyi-Gasic E et al. Plant Methods 2007;3:12 — protocol; 6-nt overhang optimal.
[MIQE09] Bustin SA et al. Clin Chem 2009;55(4):611-622. DOI 10.1373/clinchem.2008.112797 (PMID 19246619) — qPCR efficiency 90-110% acceptable.

_published_primer_exact_match.purpose: OPTIONAL exact-match layer vs a real published primer table. Absent by default — sequences are NEVER fabricated; add them only from a cited paper table.
_published_primer_exact_match.how_to_add: On any entry in `mirnas`, add one or more of: `published_rt` (full stem-loop RT primer), `published_rt_overhang` (3' 6-nt overhang only), `published_forward` (forward qPCR primer), `published_source` (citation). U/T and case are normalized before comparison.
checks_emitted: published_forward_contains_specific — published forward contains the tool's miRNA-specific region (tolerant of differing 5' tails)
_published_primer_exact_match.caveat: Exact forward-primer match only holds vs papers using the SAME universal stem-loop tail (Chen 2005 system). For different tails, rely on `published_forward_contains_specific`.

mirnas.expect_design_failure: Every forward 3' end inside the miRNA's 5' prefix at 12-15 nt ends in 5/5 G/C (TGATTGAGCC|GCGCC), rejected by the hard 3'-end GC rule (Primer3 Max End GC, forward_primer.py); at 16 nt the GC tail pushes GC%/Tm out of range. The published forward TTCCTT+TGATTGAGCCGCGCC itself ends in GCGCC, i.e. violates that rule. Kept as a documented limitation (owner decision 2026-10-08), not relaxed in the algorithm.
